en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Eighteenth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether One Sees Form with the Eye:
"Does one see form with the eye?"— Yes.
"Does one see form by means of form?
"One should not say so...
[and so on] "...Does one see form by means of form?"
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does one discern form by means of form?
One should not say so …pe…
Does one cognize form by means of form?
Yes. Is form mind-consciousness? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “One sees a visible form with the eye”? Yes.
Is there a turning back of the eye … down to … a directing of the intention toward it?
You should not say so … Is it not the case that there is no turning back of the eye … down to … no directing of the intention toward it?
“Yes.
“If there is no turning toward of the eye … [and so on] … nor any inclination, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘One sees a form with the eye.’”
“He hears a sound with the ear” … [and so on] … “he smells an odor with the nose” … [and so on] … “he tastes a flavor with the tongue” … [and so on] …
"One touches a tangible object with the body"?
Yes. "Does one touch form with form"? [No.]
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does form touch form? Yes.
"One discerns form by means of form"?
One should not say so... [etc.
... "One discerns form by means of form"?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is form mental consciousness?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
"One touches a tangible object with the body"?
Yes. "Is there turning toward of the body ... [and so on] ... is there intention of the body"? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it not the case that there is no turning over of the body … up to … no resolve?
Yes, it is.
If there is no turning of the body … [and so on] … no aspiration, then indeed,
it should not be said: “One touches a tangible object with the body” … [and so on] … It should not be so stated.
“Does one see a visible form with the eye?
… [and so on] … “Does one touch a tangible object with the body?
Yes, one does.
But has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Here, bhikkhus, with the eye a bhikkhu sees a form … with the body he touches a tangible object”?
Is this indeed a Sutta? Yes.
In that case, one sees a visible form with the eye ... [and so on] ...
"One touches a tangible object with the body.
The discussion on "one sees a form with the eye" is concluded.
The eighteenth chapter.
Its summary verse:
The Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the world of humans;
the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One.
The Blessed Buddha has no lack of compassion;
the Blessed Buddha’s excrement and urine surpass all other fragrances;
and by means of a single noble path, he realizes the four fruits of recluseship.
One passes from one jhāna to another; there is an intermediate jhāna;
having attained meditative absorption, one hears a sound.
One sees a form with the eye ... [and so on] ...
one touches a tangible object with the body.
